sampling_model.design: The design algebra fixes any finite support \(\mathcal S\subseteq\{0,1\}^{T}\) and an ex ante reshaping law \(\Pi\).  Absorption is imposed only for the adoption-order Green, graph, and adjacent-ratio corollaries.
sampling_model.units: The population identification layer uses a generic one-unit law \(P\) and supports i.i.d. sampling.  The anchor estimator theorem instead uses the published unit-indexed triangular array and permits non-i.i.d. weak dependence through \(n^{-2}\sum_{i,j}\rho_{ij}=O(n^{-q})\).
sampling_model.treatment: Treatment paths may be arbitrary binary vectors in the base algebra.  In the published-class theorem, \(\pi_i(w)=\mathbb P(W_i=w\mid\mathcal Y_i)\) is unit-specific and conditions on the full potential-outcome schedule; absorbing paths are a separate specialization.
sampling_model.overlap: The reshaping law satisfies \(\Pi_s\geq\epsilon\) on \(\mathcal S\).  The superpopulation layer assumes \(\pi_s(X)\geq c_{\pi}\), while the published-class theorem assumes \(\pi_i(s)\geq c_{\pi}\) for every reshaping-support path.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The population functional uses a generalized path propensity.  The published-class estimator corollary is proved for known unit-specific propensities, matching the anchor theorem; cross-fitted estimated-propensity or augmented full-path-mean inference is not established in this specialization.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Under unit-specific known generalized propensities, weakly dependent units, bounded second moments, a calendar-homogeneous finite-lag outcome model, and a nonsingular reshaped design, each dynamic RIPW coefficient converges to the average corresponding lag effect.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The published-class calendar-loading theorem, with the homogeneous conclusion as a corollary

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: A conventional event-study lag coefficient is a weighted average of cohort effects from its own and other relative periods.
Inverse-probability estimators of finite-memory dynamic effects are unbiased under known panel randomization, with finite-population limit theory.
Under a time-constant random-coefficient distributed-lag model, average lag coefficients can be identified in complex treatment designs.
Conventional staggered event-study regressions admit computable probability-limit diagnostics for negative weights and cross-horizon contamination.
A time-varying parameter distributed-lag model permits lag coefficients to vary with past information.

body.tldr: For any finite binary-path support, the reshaped distributed-lag fixed-effect coefficient is an exact linear functional of calendar-by-lag effects, with Gram and loading numerators determined by the general path covariance \(C_{\Pi}\).  Absorbing supports add an ordered Green representation, a graph-theoretic full-rank criterion, and an exact pointwise Cramer sign certificate.  A separate theorem carries the tensor into the unit-indexed known-propensity and weak-dependence setup of Arkhangelsky, Imbens, Lei, and Luo and recovers their homogeneous coefficient limit.  A global sign-chamber classification over all positive ratios remains open.

project_justification.gap: Published dynamic RIPW theory proves coefficient recovery for calendar-homogeneous effects under unit-specific known propensities and weakly dependent units, but does not give the calendar-specific loading tensor.  Existing event-study decompositions do not characterize counterfactual path-law reshaping for a finite-memory lag design.  Neither literature supplies an ordered combinatorial rank law or a global adjacent-ratio sign-chamber classification.
project_justification.niche: The missing objects are the support-general coefficient-by-calendar-by-causal-lag tensor, a design-only support-rank test, and, on absorbing supports, computable ordered endpoint certificates.
project_justification.fill: The note derives the tensor with the arbitrary-path covariance kernel \(C_{\Pi}\), recovers the ordered bridge kernel \(K_{\Pi}\) only under absorption, proves an absorbing-support graph criterion for full rank, supplies exact rational forward and pointwise sign certificates, and proves a calendar-varying estimator limit under the published unit-indexed sampling conditions.  It does not claim a global sign-chamber solution.

body.related_work: Arkhangelsky, Imbens, Lei, and Luo (2024) allow arbitrary treatment paths, unit-specific known propensities conditional on full potential-outcome schedules, and non-i.i.d. weakly dependent units.  The present superpopulation identification class is not their class: the two are incomparable overall, and the present class is narrower in its common-propensity and i.i.d. sampling interpretation.  The separate published-class calendar-loading theorem works directly under their Assumptions \(2.1\)--\(2.3\), extends the coefficient limit to unit- and calendar-specific lag effects, and gives their Theorem \(4.1\) conclusion under calendar homogeneity.  Sun and Abraham (2021) decompose conventional event-study coefficients rather than a reshaped finite-memory lag design.  Bojinov, Rambachan, and Shephard (2021) study finite-memory effects under known experimental assignment.  De Chaisemartin and D'Haultfoeuille (2025) retain time-constant distributed-lag effects.  Wright (2026) supplies adjacent numerical event-study diagnostics but not assignment-law reshaping, and Ailigeng, Lu, and Wang (2023) provide modeling precedent for time-varying distributed-lag coefficients without the present causal panel geometry.
body.honest_scope: The proved scope consists of arbitrary-path pair-mass identities, a support-only kernel, the path-covariance loading formula and normalization, the absorbing Green corollary, an absorbing graph-rank criterion, exact rational forward diagnostics, a pointwise adjacent-ratio Cramer certificate, and a published-class estimator limit under known unit-specific propensities.  The superpopulation and published sampling classes are kept distinct; only the separate estimator theorem recovers the published homogeneous limit.  Global sign chambers, complete inverse membership, closest-loading optimization, worst-case bounded-effect contamination, and doubly robust cross-fitted inference remain outside the proved core.
body.interpretation: The tensor \(L_{j,t,\ell}(\Pi)\) is a design-induced loading from the calendar \(t\), causal-lag \(\ell\) effect into regression coordinate \(j\); it is not itself a causal effect.  The equality for \(\theta(\Pi)\) follows from consistency, conditional mean assignment, and baseline cancellation.  For arbitrary paths the tensor is computed from \(C_{\Pi}\); adoption-order interpretations require absorption.  The graph criterion certifies whether all lag coordinates are estimable, while the determinant signs certify one specified reshaping law rather than an entire ratio chamber.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The pointwise determinant formula reduces each loading sign to an exact polynomial sign at a supplied adjacent-ratio vector, but no theorem classifies the connected sign chambers or all feasible determinant-zero frontiers over the continuous floor-constrained ratio region.  The note also does not solve the inverse image of a target tensor, certify a closest feasible loading with worst-case bounded-effect contamination, or establish cross-fitted augmented inference.
